interpretation: The public source trajectories provide successful candidate placements on 3/8 source seeds, unlike the blind library. At depth three, greedy replay already covers all three supported source worlds. The synthesized program therefore remains a fixed sequence, and no conditional branch is learned. On new target seeds 200–207, learned program, same-data kernel predictor, and source greedy replay each solve 1/8. The kernel uses 23 placement queries versus 24 for the other two; no efficiency or structural-learning gain is established.
scope: Development follow-up in catapult only, with a different target cohort from the initial screen. Do not infer a causal bank-improvement effect by comparing its 1/8 with the earlier 0/16. Public trajectory acquisition is external, shared prior data and not a measured zero-cost training process.
decision: Stop expanding finite catalog selection as a proposed novel mechanism. A next structural program-learning experiment must create program expressions/continuous arguments beyond literal replay and specify a substantive operation beyond existing program synthesis and code-transformation methods. Native HExA remains an unreproduced strong comparator.
